title: Composite Layouts in Business Central 29.0: Brand One Report End to End
summary: Business Central 29.0 enables composite layouts where branding is split into three separate parts (header/footer, theme, and body) that merge at render time instead of baking everything into one Word document. The post walks through a complete example of branding the Standard Sales Invoice report for Contoso, covering setup in both the UI and AL code.
key_points: Composite layouts split a document into a Body layout plus a reusable header/footer part and a theme part, merged when the report runs
Theme and header/footer parts must be approved before they can be assigned, and only Body subtype layouts accept them; Default and RDLC layouts do not
Defaults for theme and header/footer can be set at global, company, report and layout level, with the most specific winning, which makes multi-company branding easy
In AL, the Subtype, HeaderFooterPart and ThemePart properties configure this; theme files must be .dotx while body and header/footer files are .docx
A shared company information dataitem in Word layouts in 29.0 lets one header/footer part work across many reports
